paragraphs: Maya and Jules were leaving the newsroom when the AI assistant they had tested that afternoon appeared in a breaking-news alert. Maya pulled up their notes. "If you give it two conflicting dates, it {{mask_1}} the newer one unless you ask it to check the source," she said. "The lab says it has more evaluation logs. If it {{mask_2}} them today, I'll add them to the story." Jules scrolled through the draft. "And if those logs {{mask_3}} the lab's claim, we can publish the comparison tonight."

They stopped at a cafe to review the recording from their demo. Jules pointed to a moment where the assistant had cited a paper that did not exist. "If I'd {{mask_4}} that warning before we ran the demo, we {{mask_5}} the clip before it went into the edit," Maya said. Jules nodded. "If a chatbot {{mask_6}} a confident answer when the evidence is missing, I usually ask it to show its sources. And if it {{mask_7}} a citation that doesn't exist, I'll flag it in the notes."

Maya opened the benchmark spreadsheet on her phone. "If I {{mask_8}} on the standards panel, I'd insist on a public test set," she said. "If the company {{mask_9}} a local version for review, we could test it without uploading our notes." Jules laughed. "If the app {{mask_10}} our draft into its training pipeline, we'd have a serious privacy problem." Maya checked an older folder. "If we'd {{mask_11}} our evaluation script, we wouldn't be arguing about these scores now."

Jules compared the public benchmark with the results from their own small test. "If the benchmark {{mask_12}} more examples from different languages and devices, it would be less vulnerable to memorized answers," he said. The lab had promised to update its documentation. "If they {{mask_13}} the latest version on the public page yesterday, readers would already be checking it themselves. If they {{mask_14}} the raw data by the end of today, I'll link it in our update." Maya glanced at the draft headline. "And if the new report {{mask_15}} a mismatch between the demo and the public build, our editor will hold the headline."

Their train was due in ten minutes, so Maya sent the lab one last request for comment. Jules saved the interview transcript. "If you're going to quote the assistant, {{mask_16}} its full answer with the prompt," he said. Maya reopened the audio file. "If I {{mask_17}} enough time tomorrow, I'll check the transcript against the recording." Jules found the correction they had discussed earlier. "If you {{mask_18}} that note before we published, the clip would have been accurate from the start."

The spokesperson replied while they were boarding. The figures in the email differed slightly from the chart in the release. Maya read the message twice. "If the guest {{mask_19}} the updated chart tonight, I'll add a note before the morning edition. And if the numbers {{mask_20}} again, we'll ask for the underlying data before we change anything." Jules put his phone away. They had a long edit ahead, but at least they knew exactly what to verify first.
